title: feat(types)!: refuse both content channels on `list` and `timeline` (family D slice 3)
body:
Refs #9256 (list + timeline slice) — the two names the previous slice held for a serial constraint. Three names remain held after this, so this pull request carries **no closing keyword** and the card stays open; the PM seat ends it.

`list` and `timeline` read NEITHER content channel, so `body` and `children` become `?: never` on the TypeScript face and a by-name `retirementTombstone` refusal on the zod mirror — each **kept a MEMBER** of the mirror shape, so `zod-mirror-parity`'s key sets stay equal.

## READERSHIP was re-derived, not inherited — and that is the whole card

The previous slice's own record says its dispatch treated "no longer contested" as "therefore narrowable", and that those are **different questions**: objectui#9264 measured which declaration OWNS a bare key; family D asks which channel the renderer READS. That conflation would have narrowed `button`. So readership was measured here from scratch, with the TypeScript **compiler API** and not with grep.

One program from the repo-root `tsconfig.json` on a BUILT tree — 6011 root names, 10752 source files, 17 unresolved-module diagnostics (all `apps/site`, its Next.js `@/` aliases and one fumadocs virtual module; none under `packages/`). 1679 `.body` / `.children` reads filed under the **declared type of the receiver**.

```
TARGETS       ListSchema 0 · TimelineSchema 0
LIT CONTROLS  ButtonSchema 2 · DivSchema 2 · CardSchema 2 · ContainerSchema 1
```

⭐ **A second control, because a zero can also mean the instrument never saw the type.** The same program was asked for EVERY property read under those two declared types, and both are seen:

| type | property reads | keys read |
|---|---:|---|
| `ListSchema` | 8 | `bind`, `items`, `ordered`, `title`, `wrapperClass` |
| `TimelineSchema` | 7 | `items`, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `rowLabel` |

Neither key set contains `body` or `children`. ⇒ the zeros are readings, not blindness.

### The `any` population, attributed rather than assumed

473 channel reads resolve to an `any` receiver, and `any` reads as NEITHER — exactly the shape that hides a hit. Every one was attributed:

- all 241 destructured hits are React `children` (91 files, key counter `children` 241 / `body` 0) destructured out of `: any` props in test mocks and render helpers; the rest of the bulk is `init.body` / `mock.calls[0][1].body` on `fetch`, `err.body` on an error envelope, and `document.body`.
- `html-elements.tsx` and `semantic.tsx` read the channel LIVE, but their tag lists are `h1`…`q` / `img` / `hr` / `br` and the seven semantic sectioning tags — **neither `list` nor `timeline`** (`ul` / `ol` / `li` are HTML tag names, not the `list` registration).
- `containers.tsx` / `page.tsx`: `collectRelatedLists` and `containsAttachmentsNode` are generic `any` node walkers with no registration; the remaining reads belong to the `page:card` / `page:section` / `page:footer` / `page:sidebar` renderers, which are family C and outside this card.
- `list.tsx` reads `item.content || renderChildren(item.body)` — the **ITEM** channel, filed under `ListItem` and not under the node. An instrument that attributed that to the node would have made `list` a `body` reader and this whole change a mistake, so the item channel is pinned as still live, on both faces.

### ⭐ `timeline` has TWO readers and both were measured

The bare `timeline` key is owned by `view:timeline` — `ObjectTimelineRenderer`, declared `React.FC` of `any`. A receiver-type sweep alone would have scored it "reads neither" **for the wrong reason**, so it was attributed directly instead: `packages/plugin-timeline` contains **no** `body` / `children` read of any kind, on any receiver, in any file. The declaration this change edits types the other reader, `TimelineRenderer` (`plugin-timeline:timeline`), which passes `skipFallback: true` and stands down from the bare key.

### Generic traversers, checked separately rather than ignored

`validateChildren` in `packages/core/src/validation/schema-validator.ts` reads `schema.children || schema.body` off `SchemaNodeUnderValidation`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` reads `data.children` off the component union — both recurse or count, neither renders, and both are node-agnostic, so they are exactly as true of the 65 rows already tombstoned. `SchemaRenderer` destructures both keys OUT of the props bag it spreads, which is why an authored value rendered NOTHING: no error, no warning, no element.

## Ownership, cross-checked (corroboration, ⛔ not the readership measurement)

`pnpm check:registry-bare-names --table`, exit 0 — 1622 source files, 425 registration claims, 1 contested key (`dashboard`, neither of these two):

| bare key | owner | who stood down (`skipFallback: true`) |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | `ui:list` (sole) | `view:list` (`packages/plugin-list`) |
| `timeline` | `view:timeline` (agreed, 2 claimants naming ONE full type) | `plugin-timeline:timeline` |

## Does anything AUTHOR the tombstoned channel?

⚠️ The shipped `pnpm census:body-dialect` is **structurally blind** to both names — its `ALL_KEYS` contains neither, so its zero is a population artifact and NOT a reading (objectui#9545, filed by the previous slice against exactly this). Caught, not shipped as a green. The same scanner was re-run over the two as its population, with `div` / `card` / `page` / `button` carried as lit controls in the same pass — 7588 files:

| key | nodes | `body` | `children` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `list` | 44 | 0 | **1** |
| `timeline` | 82 | 0 | 0 |
| `div` (control) | 199 | 71 | 99 |
| `card` (control) | 258 | 50 | 129 |
| `page` (control) | 137 | 44 | 4 |
| `button` (control) | 298 | 2 | 4 |

The single hit is `skills/objectui/guides/schema-expressions.md` — a **deliberate ❌ counter-example** whose own prose says "`list` never reads `children`", inside a `jsonc` fence that `check:skill-examples` only JSON-parses. It corroborates the measurement rather than contradicting it, and `skills/**` is outside this change's file surface, so it is reported and **not edited**.

## Ablation — direction predicted in writing FIRST, both readers, and one asymmetry reported as such

Mutation proved on disk by anchor count AND blob hash; restore proved **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty AND blob hash equal to the HEAD blob); every leg under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths; working tree clean at the end. Both readers resolve the mutated files through **relative source imports** (`../zod/data-display.zod.js`, `../data-display`), so no `dist` round-trip stands between the mutation and the verdict.

| leg | mutation | reader | predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | delete the zod `body` tombstone member on `ListSchema` | pin test under vitest | RED | **RED** exit 1 — `list.body parsed green — the tombstone is not installed` |
| A1 | same | `tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.test.json` | RED | **RED** exit 2 — 2 × TS2322 in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`, on the pair name and on the key `body` itself |
| A2 | delete `body?: never` from the TS `TimelineSchema` face | `tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.test.json` | RED, TS2578 | **RED** exit 2 — TS2578 `Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive` on the pinned `timelineBody` line, plus 1 × TS2322 at parity |
| A2 | same | pin test under vitest | GREEN | **GREEN** exit 0, 733 passed — reported as NOT MEASURED, ⛔ never as a pass |

The A2 vitest green is objectui#9546's shape: `?: never` is erased before a test runs, so a vitest run of a violated tree exits 0. It is recorded here because the obvious command for "check the tombstone" gives a green that says almost nothing. The sub-prediction on A1 held: the key SET stays equal (the zod `BaseSchema` declares `body` itself), so the parity failure is a TYPE mismatch and not `UnmirroredDeclaredKeys` — which is what makes "kept a MEMBER" load-bearing rather than decorative.

## Gates

⚠️ `dispatch-gates.mjs` REFUSES for this repo by design (exit 2, `REFUSING — asked for 'objectstack-ai/objectui', but this checkout is 'objectstack-ai/objectstack'`), so the list below is hand-derived from **objectui's own** `package.json` `check:*` scripts and `.github/workflows/`. Exit codes captured by redirect-then-capture, ⛔ never through a pipe. Heavy runs serialized through the shared verify lock.

| gate | command | exit |
|---|---|---|
| Build | `turbo run build --filter='!@object-ui/site'` — 43/43 | 0 |
| Type Check (repo-wide, **forced**) | `turbo run type-check --force` — 81/81, `Cached: 0 cached, 81 total` | 0 |
| Lint (repo-wide) | `pnpm lint` — 47/47, `Cached: 0 cached` | 0 |
| Test — `packages/types` | 191 files, 4553 tests | 0 |
| Test — the family-D pin, verbose | 733 tests; both new rows and all five live controls executing | 0 |
| Test — `components` · `cli` · `plugin-list` · `plugin-timeline` · `core` | 552 files, 7513 tests | 0 |
| CLI self-check on this repo | `pnpm check` — `All checks passed` | 0 |
| Doc snippets | 670 of 670 blocks judged against the BUILT types | 0 |
| Doc examples | 124 blocks, 89 failing exactly as their ledger rows declare | 0 |
| Doc component types · doc fences · doc example ids | | 0 |
| Skill examples | every marked skill fence holds up against the built types | 0 |
| Control Byte Scan | 7739 tracked text files | 0 |
| Line Citation Gate | 0 new cross-file citations | 0 |
| Changeset presence · changeset fixed | 3 published source files, 1 changeset | 0 |
| `check:registry-bare-names` · `check:sdui-registration-pins` · `check:prompt-keys` · `check:component-surface-parity` | | 0 |

No gate answered the unbuilt-package sentinel (`exit 2 [unbuilt-package]`), and no gate was read through a pipe.

**Coverage proof, counted rather than assumed:** `packages/types/tsconfig.json` does NOT include the pin test and `tsconfig.test.json` does — `tsc --listFiles` answers 0 and 1 respectively, which is what makes the `@ts-expect-error` block a real assertion under `pnpm type-check`.

Not run locally, left to CI: the 4-way `pnpm test` shards beyond the six packages above, `test:dist`, E2E, Bundle Analysis.

## What is NOT in this change

`button` and `app-schema-renderer` are family **C** — a LIVE `body || children` fallback, the maintainer's call on objectui#8284. `input` is family **E**, frozen: `InputShorthandSchema` is an `Omit` of it, so a tombstone propagates onto the `any`-typed shorthand faces. All three are untouched, and the pin test's `button` live control keeps proving it.

## Acceptance notes — out of scope, not fixed here

- `packages/components/src/renderers/data-display/list.tsx` registers `list` with an authoring input whose description reads `Array of strings or objects with content/body`, pointing an author (or an AI) at `items[].body` — a key the published `ListItem` face does not declare (an excess-property error) and `ListItemSchema` silently strips, since it is a plain `z.object`. The renderer really does read it, so the metadata and the two published faces disagree about the item channel. Reported for triage; ⛔ untouched here because it is the ITEM channel and outside this card's ruling.
- `ListSchema.dividers` and `ListSchema.dense` are declared on both faces and read by nothing — the same ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove shape `TimelineSchema.events` / `orientation` / `position` already carry in their own docblocks. Noted, not filed: successor is the ADR-0049 route those three are already on.

Instruments, their outputs and the written predictions live in this run's scratchpad; every figure above is a reading taken on this branch, ⛔ not a figure carried from the card or the dispatch.
